data.title: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbs to highest level since 2007 ahead of Fed decision
data.description:
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield (US10Y) climbed to its highest level in nearly two decades, extending a global bond selloff driven by surging energy prices, rising debt, and inflation concerns.

The benchmark yield rose as much as 4 basis points from the session low of 4.99% to 5.03% on Tuesday, surpassing its 2023 peak and reaching its highest level since 2007. On Monday, the 10-year yield had briefly crossed 5%, before sliding a little.

The latest move followed a rise in global oil prices as risks to Middle East energy supplies increased.

The bond-market selloff adds pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision Wednesday, with investors expecting officials to raise short-term borrowing costs for the first time since July 2023.

If the Fed does not hike, or if Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh signals less tightening ahead than currently priced into money markets, bond investors could demand even higher yields to compensate for rising inflation risks.

The rise extended across the Treasury curve, with the rate-sensitive U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) gaining 3 basis points to about 4.69%, while the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) climbed 4 basis points to 5.39%.

data.title: UK's unemployment holds at 4.9%
data.description:
• The UK unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.9% in the three months to July 2026, remaining below expectations for a rise to 5.0%.
  • The number of unemployed people rose by 11,000 from the previous quarter to 1.778M. The inactivity rate edged down to 20.9%, while people with second jobs rose to 1.283M.

data.title: China hits back at AI slowdown push, calls it ‘fearmongering’
data.description:
China has pushed back against calls to slow AI development and restrict its access to advanced AI technology, calling the campaign “fearmongering” and warning that it could fuel confrontation with the U.S.

“Fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance which serves no one's interest,” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday in response to Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei’s call for a global slowdown in AI development.

Amodei has warned that a “Chinese lead in AI would pose grave danger for the United States and the world” and called for continued restrictions on sales to China of the most advanced AI chips and chipmaking equipment.

China’s state-run Global Times also attacked Amodei’s proposal, saying it was “packed with containment provisions targeting China” and was “in essence, a ‘Cold War playbook’ for the AI sector.” The newspaper said the underlying agenda was “to attempt to curb China's AI development through technological barriers.”

The dispute underscores the growing tensions between Washington and Beijing over AI. U.S. President Donald Trump is expected to discuss AI governance with Chinese President Xi Jinping at a meeting planned for late September.

data.title: GSK expands myeloma pipeline in deal worth up to $750M
data.description:
• GSK (GSK) has agreed to acquire full global rights to Chimagen Biosciences’ trispecific T-cell engager program for multiple myeloma in a deal worth up to $750M.
  • GSK (GSK) will pay an upfront fee for full global rights, with Chimagen eligible for success-based milestones. Chimagen's trispecific TCE targets T cells and two tumour-associated antigens simultaneously.
  • The program is expected to enter phase I clinical trials in 2027.
  • The deal builds on a prior GSK-Chimagen agreement covering CMG1A46, a dual CD19/CD20 TCE in phase I.

data.title: Kestra targets $141M FY 2027 revenue and mid-70% gross margin in next few years as Q1 revenue reaches $31M
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Kestra Medical Technologies (KMTS) Q1 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • “Revenue advanced sequentially off a strong fourth quarter and grew 60% year-over-year to $31 million,” said (Founder, President, CEO & Director Brian Webster), alongside “gross margin of 56.5%,” which he said marked “the 11th quarter in a row of sequential gross margin expansion.”

  • Webster raised the company’s longer-term gross margin target, saying, “we are increasingly confident that Kestra can achieve mid-70s gross margin percentage in the next few years,” and noted this was “a meaningful increase from our previously communicated target of 70%.”

  • Webster described a near-term operating focus on scaling through automation, outlining an AI road map tied to operating KPIs across “patient support and adherence,” “revenue access and collections,” and “commercial demand acceleration,” with the goal of “increased rep productivity as measured by patient fittings per rep without requiring a proportional increase in headcount.”

  • (Chief Financial Officer Vaseem Mahboob) summarized revenue drivers as “continued WCD market expansion, competitive share gains, a higher mix of in-network patients and ongoing improvements in our revenue cycle management capabilities,” adding, “we continue to see improvements in all 3 key drivers of our revenue model, our prescription bill rate, our bill rate and our collections performance.”

Outlook

  • Mahboob updated full-year guidance: “We expect revenue of $141 million, representing growth of 48% compared to fiscal year 2026. This compares to prior fiscal year 2027 revenue guidance of $137 million.”

  • On growth drivers embedded in that outlook, Mahboob said, “We expect fittings growth to be driven by deeper penetration within existing accounts and the activation of new accounts as we invest in the regional coverage,” and “growth in revenue per fit to be driven by a higher mix of in-network patients and continued investments in our rev cycle management capabilities.”

  • Management reiterated expectations for second-half acceleration. Mahboob said, “we do expect those reps to ramp up here in the second half of the year. So we expect the second half to be faster than the first half.”

  • Relative to the prior quarter, Kestra increased FY 2027 revenue guidance to $141 million from $137 million, and Webster’s margin outlook shifted to “mid-70s” from a prior “70%” target.

Financial Results

  • Kestra reported “total revenue was $31 million,” and Mahboob said gross margin “increased to 56.5% in the first quarter versus 45.7% in the prior year period,” attributing the improvement to “an increase in revenue per fit from more in-network patients and a decline in cost per fit driven by volume leverage and execution of cost improvement projects.”

  • Mahboob detailed expense and profitability items: “GAAP operating expenses were $55.2 million,” including “$1.4 million of nonrecurring items related to a Biobeat milestone payment and onetime professional fees related to a key R&D project.” He added, “GAAP net loss was $44.1 million,” and “adjusted EBITDA loss was $24 million.”

  • On cash and liquidity, Mahboob said, “our cash used from operating activities in the first quarter was $32.3 million,” noting it was “higher on a sequential basis, driven by payout of our company-wide bonus and timing of payments to suppliers,” and added, “cash, cash equivalents and investments totaled $245 million,” with “liquidity of approximately $320 million” including unused term-loan availability.

  • Mahboob emphasized balance-sheet capacity after financing announced in July: “a new $200 million term loan facility,” which he called “non-dilutive financing,” and said it “fortifies our balance sheet, reduces our cost of capital and provides a significant financial flexibility to invest in our commercial strategies and expand our fleet.”

Q&A

  • Larry Biegelsen, Wells Fargo: asked why Kestra “raise[d] by more than the beat this quarter” and about cadence; (CFO Mahboob) responded that key KPIs “are all tracking in the right direction” and reiterated that “we expect the second half to be faster than the first half.”

  • Larry Biegelsen, Wells Fargo: asked for an update on Biobeat and the “new pipeline product”; (CEO Webster) said, “We’re not quite ready to do that yet,” but added the aim is to “extend that platform” with “a capability that doesn’t exist in WCD today.”

  • Matthew O’Brien, Piper Sandler: pressed on why management raised the long-term margin view to “mid-70s”; (CFO Mahboob) cited “reduction in cost per fit,” “improvements in revenue per fit” driven by in-network mix, and expected “volume growth.”

  • Michael Polark, Wolfe Research: asked to frame the revenue outperformance by volume vs. revenue per fit; (CFO Mahboob) said Kestra is “obviously not commenting” on prior conversion disclosures but stated “continued improvement in all of the KPIs that drive the revenue model.”

  • Michael Polark, Wolfe Research: asked about the significance of a large payer expanding non-ischemic coverage; (CEO Webster) said, “Among the large payers, I would say this was the outlier,” and added there are “other regional and smaller payers” with similar prior positions.

  • Marie Thibault, BTIG: asked whether elevated R&D spend persists and about AI timeline; (CEO Webster) said the expenses were “onetime in nature” and “the R&D expense line will go back down,” while (CFO Mahboob) said Kestra expects “GAAP OpEx for the year to be at $220 million,” with R&D “somewhere in the 5% to 7% range in the second half of the year,” and AI-driven leverage is “in outer years, not this year.”

  • Frederick Wise, Stifel: asked whether anything “unusually strong or onetime” drove Q1 revenue and about quarterly cadence; (CFO Mahboob) replied “there’s nothing different this year than last year” and again pointed to rep ramp dynamics and a faster second half.

  • Stephanie Elghazi (for Travis Steed), BofA: asked about market expansion and market share; (CEO Webster) said the market “is definitely accelerating,” and added, “we think in this most recent quarter, we’re somewhere around 15% market share in the U.S. market.”

  • Suraj Kalia, Oppenheimer: asked about AI improving “fittings per rep”; (CEO Webster) said it is about “free up time,” better territory prioritization, and added, “the path to profitability… runs right through rep productivity.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive but probing on the durability of guidance and the mechanics behind margin and cadence, including repeated attempts to parse “cadence,” “portion of that beat,” and whether Q1 contained “onetime” elements.

  • Management’s tone was positive and confident in targets and execution; Webster said, “we are increasingly confident,” “we’re excited,” and “we’re certainly bullish on our story,” while finance answers were more guarded on disclosure detail (Mahboob: “we are not commenting”).

  • Versus the prior quarter, the current call carried higher confidence on margin trajectory (explicitly moving from a 70% target to “mid-70s”) and introduced more explicit timing on AI leverage (Webster: “accelerate in FY ’28 and ’29”), while analyst questioning remained centered on cadence, profitability trajectory, and drivers of guidance.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Guidance shifted up to $141 million from $137 million, with management attributing confidence to KPIs “tracking in the right direction,” continued in-network expansion, and sales force ramp expected to lift the second half.

  • Long-term margin framing became more aggressive: Q4 framed “70% plus gross margins,” while Q1 stated “mid-70s… in the next few years,” with Mahboob later adding, “we’re not talking about mid-70s in 5 years. We’re talking about mid-70s in the next 2 to 3 years.”

  • Commercial execution commentary evolved from Q4’s emphasis on expanding territory count and training investments to Q1’s emphasis on splitting “high-volume platinum territories,” rep ramp speed, and AI-enabled rep productivity.

  • Analyst focus was consistent across both calls (cadence, conversion/RCM, margin progression), but the Q1 discussion included more direct questioning on the composition of revenue performance and a payer-policy change for non-ischemic coverage.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management flagged execution risk around scaling: Webster said automation is needed to avoid “human volume-based G&A investment,” and positioned technology investments as a way to “bend the operating expense curve as transaction volumes continue to grow.”

  • Profitability and cash burn remained an investor focus; Mahboob said Q1 burn was “higher on a sequential basis” due to timing items, and management expects burn “to decline sequentially throughout fiscal year 2027.”

  • Product and pipeline visibility remained limited ahead of next quarter; Webster said the company is “not quite ready” to provide more detail on the late-stage R&D effort, though Kestra expects to discuss it “in the next quarter.”

Final Takeaway

Kestra management highlighted Q1 revenue of $31 million and 56.5% gross margin, raised FY 2027 revenue guidance to $141 million, and increased its longer-term gross margin ambition to “mid-70s… in the next few years.” Executives tied the outlook to second-half acceleration from sales-rep ramp, higher in-network mix and RCM improvements, and a push toward AI and automation aimed at rep productivity and scaling operating costs, while remaining guarded on disclosing detailed volume-to-revenue mechanics until year-end.

data.title: Trump’s approval recovers from record low, but Democrats gain edge in Congress: Reuters
data.description:
• President Donald ​Trump's public approval rating rose from a record low, while Americans voiced growing support for Democrats gaining ‌power in the U.S. Congress in a Reuters/Ipsos poll taken in the days after the Republican Party's first-ever midterm convention last week.
  • The four-day poll showed 63% of Americans - including four in 10 Republicans and nine in 10 Democrats - disapproved of Trump's offer made in his ​convention speech that he would ensure all Americans get a $5,000 dividend if Republicans retain control of the ​U.S. Congress in November's midterm elections.
  • The survey gathered responses from 1,143 Americans nationwide and had ⁠a margin of error of 3 percentage points in either direction.
  • Some 35% of Americans give Trump a thumbs ​up for his performance in the White House, up from 33% in an August 28 to 31 Reuters/Ipsos poll, the ​lowest of his political career.
  • Asked which party they would vote for if the congressional elections were held today in what is known as ‌a "generic ⁠ballot" poll, 44% picked Democrats and 37% picked Republicans. The 7-point gap was the widest since Trump returned to the White House in January 2025.
  • Trump's construction projects throughout the U.S. capital - including a ballroom for the White House - ⁠were largely ​polarizing and viewed through a partisan lens, with 91% of Democrats ​in the survey saying they opposed the plans, compared to one in four Republicans who were against them. Some two-thirds of Americans - including half of ​Republicans - considered the construction projects to be a low priority.

data.title: CrowdStrike CEO Kurtz: ‘The genie’s out of the bottle’ on AI threats
data.description:
CrowdStrike (CRWD) CEO George Kurtz pushed back on calls to slow the development of advanced AI, saying the technology—and the security risks it creates—are already here.

“The genie’s out of the bottle,” Kurtz said, pointing to frontier and open-weight models that are already available. He said slowing future development would not address threats from systems already in use. “Pacing what comes next doesn’t secure what’s already here,” he said in a post responding to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.

Kurtz added that AI is giving “every criminal and lone actor elite execution,” making cyberattacks faster and more accessible. He said AI agents should be treated as privileged identities, with strict permissions, short-lived credentials and a kill switch, while humans remain in control of high-stakes decisions.

Kurtz also called for closer cooperation between AI developers and cybersecurity firms. He said Anthropic (ANTHRO) and OpenAI (OPENAI) should work with independent evaluators and offered CrowdStrike’s threat intelligence to the effort. OpenAI (OPENAI) CEO Sam Altman has separately said the industry needs to “pace the frontier.”

data.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump bid to restrict mail-in voting
data.description:
The Supreme Court has rejected President Donald Trump’s effort to restrict mail-in ballots for the midterm elections, ending a wave of last-minute legal challenges as voting gets underway.

The decision on Monday allows states to continue sending out mail ballots under the same processes they’ve used for years and have accounted for nearly a third of votes cast.

It represented a stark defeat for Trump on an issue he consistently has emphasized as vital to ensuring election integrity even though there is virtually no evidence of fraud with mail ballots.

The Supreme Court majority wrote that the administration’s push to implement the restrictions this year is likely to lose in court, though the brief emergency order didn’t detail its reasoning. Two justices, Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas, publicly dissented.

The Trump administration had asked the justices, once again at the center of a roiling political controversy, to clear the way for restrictions before the pivotal November contests for control of Congress.

Alito wrote in his dissent that the Postal Service “has broad authority to regulate the mail” and likely does have the power to enforce Trump’s restrictions.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh, meanwhile, agreed that the restrictions should not go into effect for the midterms but indicated he might rule in favor of the Trump administration if the issue comes back before the court at a later time.

Mail ballots are already being sent to voters

Election officials have said there was simply no way to carry out a complete overhaul in the weeks before the midterms. Indeed, Alabama, North Carolina and Wisconsin began sending mail ballots to voters over the past week while the new system was still not active.

The Trump administration plan would require states to adopt a uniform envelope style and submit lists of eligible voters to an online portal. The Postal Service could refuse to deliver ballots to states that didn’t comply.

data.title: Trump calls AI a ‘hoax’ in surprise onstage call with Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump dismissed concerns over AI as a “hoax” during a surprise phone call with Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on Monday as debate over whether AI development should be slowed intensifies.

Huang put Trump on speakerphone before the live audience. Trump said, “The robots will not be taking over. The AI will not be taking over the rest of the world. The whole thing is a hoax.”

Trump added, "The data centers are great. They make people wealthy. They make states wealthy. AI is bigger than the internet. These people are playing right into the hands of China. We're not going to let that happen."

Huang agreed with Trump, saying, “You’re right, we’re not going to let that happen, sir.”

Trump has also said the U.S. already has regulatory and criminal powers over AI companies and accused critics of creating a “sick conspiracy” against AI and data centers.

Speaking at the summit, Huang praised former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who resigned over AI safety concerns, calling him courageous and saying whistleblowers should be taken seriously.

Huang also said the debate had created a false choice between fast AI innovation and safety, as calls to slow development have grown following Coxon’s resignation.

The comments come as OpenAI (OPENAI) CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Elon Musk have raised concerns over AI risks and called for stronger safeguards or slower development. Trump has rejected those calls, saying the U.S. already has sufficient regulatory tools, and tighter oversight could hurt its lead over China.

data.title: Bitcoin rally hits pause as Clarity Act odds slide
data.description:
The odds of the Clarity Act being passed this year, which had risen above 30% on Polymarket during US trading hours, dropped back to 18% early Tuesday in Asia.

That saw Bitcoin (BTC-USD) — which accounts for around 60% of the market value of all cryptocurrencies — retreat from as high as $79,586 to below $78,000, and was last trading at $77,578.33. A rally in crypto markets has stalled as optimism wanes that a key US regulatory bill will progress this week.

US Senator Mark Warner told reporters at the US Capitol that a group of Democratic negotiators would send a counteroffer to Republicans ahead of the pivotal procedural vote on the Clarity Act, the comprehensive crypto regulation bill that has been stuck in partisan wrangling for a year, Bloomberg News reported.

The bill will need a number of Democrats to cross party lines to advance and move later to final passage thanks to the Senate’s 60-vote rule for most legislation.

“Odds of a 2026 signing sat above 70% in May, collapsed to the low teens through August and rebounded toward 30% on Monday. That is a market with no stable read,” said Rachael Lucas, an analyst at BTC Markets, citing prediction-market odds. Still, “a counteroffer is consistent with a negotiation that is still live, not one that has broken down,” she added, as per the report.
